title: Progressive Exposure Controller: environment-aware rollout automation for Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a controller that automates progressive exposure (canary, A/B, and shadow paths) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while enforcing per-environment constraints (network, KMS access, capacity quotas, and fallback rules). The controller should translate high-level rollout intents (percent schedules, hold gates, evaluation sets) into environment-safe admission policies and provide deterministic rollback triggers tied to performance, correctness, and cost signals.
acceptance_criteria: Policy templates exist for Hosted/Dedicated/Private mapping high-level intents to concrete admission rules
Controller can execute a 4-step canary schedule (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with metric-based gates and automatic rollback if any gate fails
Private deployments enforce no-remote-fallback flag and honor on-prem timeouts; attempts to route off-cluster are rejected with audit log entry
Dedicated deployments respect reserved GPU quotas and fail open to pre-configured variant (e.g., quantized model) only when allowed by project policy
Shadow traffic can be enabled with configurable sampling and redaction/transformation hooks and no user-visible latency impact
End-to-end e2e test harness validates rollback on: latency P95 spike > 40%, error-rate > 3x baseline, embedding quality regression on held prompts
Console shows per-route exposure budget, current weights, and last gate evaluation with links to traces
design_decisions: Use a declarative Rollout CRD-like spec stored in the control plane that contains per-environment overrides (hard limits and allowed fallbacks).
Separate translator (intent->policy) from executor (admission/enforcer) so Hosted can use dynamic fallback while Private uses stricter local-only enforcement.
Implement exposure budget accounting (requests/sec or tokens/sec) to avoid saturating Dedicated reserved capacity during ramp phases.
Add an evaluation adapter that can run lightweight prompt sets against the candidate and baseline in quiet mode (shadow) and surface quality deltas as a gate signal.
Rollback semantics will be automated and reversible: on trigger, immediately stop new exposure and either promote previous stable or shift traffic to pre-authorized fallback variant.
Metrics gates are windowed and use both absolute thresholds and relative deltas to reduce false positives from noisy signals.
implementation_notes: Components: rollout-translator, env-policy-store, exposure-enforcer (admission layer), metrics-gate, evaluation-adapter, audit-logger.
Hosted path: allow model-variant fallback to cheaper quantized variant unless project config sets fallback: deny.
Dedicated path: consult reserved-capacity API; enforce exposure budget and reject ramp step if pool headroom < required tokens/sec.
Private path: honor no-remote-fallback and k8s taints for air-gapped clusters; translator emits explicit deny rules for cross-cluster routing.
Admission hooks will attach decision metadata to requests for traceability (policy_id, rollout_id, step).
Performance: implement lightweight in-memory caches for policy lookups; warm-up policy cache on rollout start to avoid initial latencies.
Schema: rollout spec supports weighted-variants[], shadow{enabled, sample_pct, transformer}, steps[{percent, min_duration, gates}], hold_on_gate_failure boolean.
Backwards compat: support existing traffic-split v1 API by emitting compatibility mappings from Rollout spec.
testing_plan: Unit tests for translator edge cases: private-disallow-fallback, dedicated-capacity-shortfall, hosted-dynamic-fallback.
Simulation harness that replays production traffic traces with varying seq lengths to validate exposure budget accounting.
Canary e2e: run full 4-step ramp in staging across all three environment types and assert gates and audit logs.
Chaos tests: inject synthetic latency and error spikes to ensure rollback triggers and that previous stable remains reachable.
Quality regression test: run held prompt set in shadow and compute embedding/LLM response similarity metrics; fail rollout if quality delta exceeds threshold.
Security test: verify Private path cannot access hosted-only KMS endpoints; run network policy verification.
Manual runbook review with SRE and Security before first production rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): deploy controller to staging control plane, run 2 internal canaries with dev traffic for 48h.
Phase B (beta-hosted): enable Hosted canaries with percent schedule 1%->5%->20%->100% over 72h with 30m evaluation windows.
Phase C (dedicated): run canary against a dedicated pool with exposure budget caps; require manual approval if reserved capacity utilization > 70%.
Phase D (private): allow tenant opt-in; default no-remote-fallback; rollout only after tenant security signoff; step durations longer (48h per step) to account for slower telemetry.
Phase E: enable automated A/B experiments via router that can serve sticky user buckets and report baseline/candidate deltas to experiments dashboard.
Communication: release notes, runbooks, Slack channel #rollout-controller and scheduled review with Solutions Eng.
rollback_criteria: Latency: P95 exceeds baseline by > 40% for 3 consecutive windows
Errors: 5xx rate increases to > 3x baseline or absolute > 2% for 15 minutes
Quality: held-prompt similarity drops below threshold (configured per model) or regression count > 5%
Cost anomaly: per-token cost increases by > 50% and projected monthly delta > $5000 for that customer segment
Security: audit detects any routing that violates no-remote-fallback in Private deployments
Manual: SRE or PM can trigger immediate rollback via Console with one-click revert and annotated reason.
observability_requirements: Per-rollout metrics: current step, target percent, actual percent, exposure_budget_used, metric_gate_scores
Traces: attach policy decision id and rollout metadata to request traces
Logs: audit entries for any denied routing decision, fallback events, and automatic rollback triggers
Dashboards: per-customer and global rollout heatmap, quality-regression timelines, capacity headroom for Dedicated pools
Alerts: PagerDuty for auto-rollback event and SLO breach; low-severity alerts for gate failures that are transient.
comments: 2026-02-15: Initial spike complete. Evaluated three translation strategies (static mapping, rules engine, policy DSL). Team aligned on policy DSL for expressivity. - Ava
2026-02-28: Implemented translator prototype and basic admission hook. Observed 6ms median extra latency on cold policy lookup; added warm cache to mitigate. - Ravi
2026-03-04: Design review with Security: Private must surface explicit audit events for any attempted cross-cluster routing; added audit-logger requirement. - Security
2026-03-08: SRE feedback: dedicated exposure cap should be tied to reserved tokens/sec API rather than a static percentage. Adjusted plan. - Priya (SRE)
2026-03-11: QA reported flakiness in shadow transformer when payload redaction rules mismatch tenant schema. Added schema validation and fallback to drop-shadow mode. - QA
